name: @crela/mcp

tools.name: search_software
tools.description: Search the Crela marketplace for approved software, apps and games. Public, no API key required. Returns only approved, publicly listed tools — use list_my_software to see your own pending/rejected/unlisted tools. Use limit (1-50) to control how many results come through and keep the response small; page through the rest with page.

query.description: Full-text search over title and description

lang.description: Filter by the language of the software user interface, e.g. "de". Not the programming language.

page.description: 1-based page for paging through more results (see total_pages in the response) instead of pulling everything at once

limit.description: How many results come through, 1-50 (server default 20). Lower it to a short shortlist to keep the response small; then get_software for the full detail of one.

tools.name: get_software
tools.description: Fetch the full public detail of one approved software item by its slug. Only works for publicly approved tools — use list_my_software to find your own tools by id.

tools.name: get_submission_requirements
tools.description: Return the machine-readable submission rules (required fields, KO rules, bundle rules). Call this before submit_new_software so a build passes review. Public, no API key required. Recommended workflow for a new submission: 1. get_submission_requirements (this tool) → 2. preview_marker (paid tools only, embed CRELA_SDK_MARKER before building) → 3. precheck_build (dry-run gate check, catches problems before wasting a review slot) → 4. submit_new_software (creates the listing and starts review; pass the storage_path from step 3 to skip a second upload) → 5. upload_screenshot (at least 2 screenshots of at least 640 x 360 px; an approved tool is listed only once they are in. A square logo of at least 256 x 256 px is recommended; optionally upload_clip for a short MP4 preview clip) → 6. check_review_status (poll every 30 s until review_job_status is not "queued"/"running") → 7. get_review_report (read full findings after completion). For subsequent releases of an existing tool: 1. get_sdk_marker (paid tools: fetch current marker for the existing software_id) → 2. precheck_build → 3. update_software → 4. check_review_status (poll until complete). Never use submit_new_software for a tool that already exists.

tools.name: list_my_software
tools.description: List all software you own with its id, slug, review status (pending/approved/rejected/flagged), whether it is unlisted, price and sales count. Use this to recover the software_id needed by update_software, check_review_status, set_metadata and delete_software. Unlike search_software, this also returns pending, rejected and unlisted tools. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: precheck_build
tools.description: Dry-run the submit gate on a build ZIP WITHOUT creating a listing or a review. Runs the same deterministic checks as a real submission: framework detection, bundle completeness (required lockfiles/sidecars/manifests per framework x OS), the SDK marker KO-10 for paid tools, and the file-count limit. This is NOT the full review — it does not run virus/CVE scan, sandbox or the LLM agent. Does NOT count toward the 5/24 h rate limit. Call it as often as needed until gate passes. Response: { gate: "pass"|"fail", framework, platforms, entrypoint, sdk_marker: { required, satisfied }, code?, message? }. On fail: code and message explain exactly what to fix. On sdk_marker.satisfied=false: embed CRELA_SDK_MARKER in the build env and rebuild. Always call this before submit_new_software or update_software. The response also carries storage_path: pass that to submit_new_software or update_software instead of file_path and the same ZIP is not uploaded a second time. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the build ZIP on disk. Omit when passing storage_path.

storage_path.description: storage_path from a previous precheck_build response - reuses that upload instead of sending the same ZIP again.

slug.description: The planned or existing tool slug (needed for the per-slug SDK marker check)

price_eur.description: 0 for free, > 0 for paid. Paid tools require the embedded SDK marker.

framework.description: Override; auto-detected from the ZIP if omitted

license.description: Open source only: the SPDX identifier of the license, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-only. Omit it for the Crela Standard EULA. The product page then names the license, and it takes precedence over the Crela license terms. The ZIP must contain the license text as LICENSE or COPYING. Copyleft licenses (GPL, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, EPL, EUPL) also need exactly one archive with the complete source of this build in the folder crela-source/ of the ZIP (Crela offers it next to the download, it is not installed), and such tools can only be free for now. An open source license can only be set with the first submission.

tools.name: preview_marker
tools.description: Compute the per-tool SDK marker (KO-10) for a NOT-yet-created tool from its planned slug. Paid tools (price > 0) must embed this marker via the build env var CRELA_SDK_MARKER before building and submitting. For tools that already exist use get_sdk_marker (needs software_id, not slug). Returns { marker, slug, slug_available }. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

slug.description: The planned URL slug of the tool you are about to submit

tools.name: get_sdk_marker
tools.description: Fetch the per-tool SDK marker (KO-10) of an EXISTING tool by software_id. Embed it via the build env var CRELA_SDK_MARKER before uploading a new build with update_software. For a tool that does not exist yet use preview_marker (needs slug, not software_id). Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: submit_new_software
tools.description: Submit a brand-new software listing to Crela and start its review. Use this only for the FIRST submission of a tool that has never existed before. DO NOT use this to upload a newer version of a tool that already exists — use update_software for that. Always run precheck_build first to catch gate failures before wasting a review slot. entrypoint, framework, platforms, os and arch are auto-detected from the ZIP - pass them only when detection is wrong or the server reports an ambiguous entrypoint. Returns { tool: { id, slug, ... }, tool_review_id, build_id: null, warnings? }. Use tool.id as software_id for check_review_status, update_software, set_metadata and all other subsequent calls. The review starts asynchronously — poll check_review_status until complete. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the build ZIP on disk. Omit when passing storage_path.

storage_path.description: storage_path from a previous precheck_build response - reuses that upload instead of sending the same ZIP again.

description.description: Short description, min. 20 characters, no URLs

long_description.description: Long description, min. 80 characters, no URLs

price_eur.description: 0 for free, or at least 0.50 (the smallest amount our payment provider can charge)

version.description: Semver, e.g. "1.0.0". A first submission takes no pre-release suffix.

categories.description: Required: 1 to 3 categories, the first is the main one. No default.

license.description: Open source only: the SPDX identifier of the license, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0-only. Omit it for the Crela Standard EULA. The product page then names the license, and it takes precedence over the Crela license terms. The ZIP must contain the license text as LICENSE or COPYING. Copyleft licenses (GPL, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, EPL, EUPL) also need exactly one archive with the complete source of this build in the folder crela-source/ of the ZIP (Crela offers it next to the download, it is not installed), and such tools can only be free for now. An open source license can only be set with the first submission.

tool_languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of every language the software user interface is available in, e.g. ["en","de"]. NOT the programming language. Defaults to ["de"] - set it deliberately, it drives the lang filter in search_software.

privacy_policy.description: Privacy policy text. Required in practice for anything with analytics or telemetry: KO_09 rejects a build whose code talks to a tracking service that the policy does not name.

support_contact.description: Support contact shown to buyers, e.g. an email address

security_updates_until.description: Required for paid tools, optional for free tools (a free tool without it is listed as coming without a commitment to security updates). Date until which you provide security updates (YYYY-MM-DD), at least two years from today; five years recommended (the EU Cyber Resilience Act expects five for most software from 2027-12-11). Shown to buyers before they buy

safety_notes.description: Warnings and safety information buyers need, e.g. flashing lights or changes to system settings (plain text, max 2000 characters). Shown on the product page

network_mode.description: Required (Crela Creator Terms § 3 (1)). Network allowlist mode: "none" = the app needs no network, "declared" = it only talks to the hosts in network_hosts, "user_chosen" = the user picks the servers (SSH, database, RSS or download clients). The Crela launcher starts the app behind a local proxy that logs every connection and blocks hosts outside the list; with "user_chosen" nothing is blocked.

network_hosts.description: Hosts your app connects to, e.g. ["api.example.com", "*.cdn.example.com"]. A wildcard covers subdomains of your own domain only. Every host that receives user or device data must also be named in privacy_policy (KO_09).

confirm_build_declarations.description: Required for every build (Crela Creator Terms § 3 (5)). Set true only if all of this is true for the build: It does not update itself. No code, bundled program or script downloads, installs or runs new versions or additional program code. New versions reach customers only through Crela. It sells nothing past Crela. No upgrades, licenses, subscriptions, plans, plugins or in-app currency for this app are sold anywhere else. Its network declaration is complete. It lists every server the app contacts on its own, and every transfer of personal data to these servers is described in my privacy policy. It is not export-controlled. It does not break or weaken encryption, it is not made to monitor, intercept or secretly access the communications or devices of others, and users cannot add their own encryption or change how it works beyond the settings it offers. Standard encryption, for example HTTPS, encrypted files or a password manager, is fine. If one of these points does not hold for your app, write to contact@crela.io before you submit it.

entrypoint.description: Path to the main binary inside the ZIP; auto-detected. Set it when the server reports the entrypoint is ambiguous (VALIDATION error with candidates).

framework.description: Override; auto-detected from the ZIP if omitted

os.description: Target OS of this build; derived from the detected platforms if omitted

arch.description: CPU architecture; default x86_64; x64/amd64 and arm64 aliases accepted

tools.name: update_software
tools.description: Replace the build binary of an EXISTING software with a new version. Use this when a tool already exists and you want to ship a new release or demo build. DO NOT use this for a brand-new tool that has never been submitted — use submit_new_software for that. To change only metadata (title, price, description) without uploading a binary, use set_metadata instead. Use list_my_software to recover the software_id if you do not have it. Handles the presign → direct R2 upload → finalize flow, so large builds do not hit the upload timeout. Sending channel "release" puts the tool back into review; channel "demo" publishes a demo build without touching the live listing. Rate limit: 5 updates per tool per 24 h (shared with set_metadata); this tool checks the budget before uploading, so an exhausted quota costs you nothing. check_review_status shows the remaining budget. Pass the storage_path from precheck_build instead of file_path to avoid uploading the same ZIP twice. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the build ZIP on disk. Omit when passing storage_path.

storage_path.description: storage_path from a previous precheck_build response - reuses that upload instead of sending the same ZIP again.

version.description: Semver, e.g. "1.7.5". A pre-release suffix such as "1.0.0-beta.1" is allowed here.

arch.description: CPU architecture; x64/amd64 and arm64 aliases are accepted

entrypoint.description: Path to the main binary inside the ZIP; auto-detected if omitted

change_message.description: Changelog note shown to buyers after approval

confirm_build_declarations.description: Required for every build (Crela Creator Terms § 3 (5)). Set true only if all of this is true for the build: It does not update itself. No code, bundled program or script downloads, installs or runs new versions or additional program code. New versions reach customers only through Crela. It sells nothing past Crela. No upgrades, licenses, subscriptions, plans, plugins or in-app currency for this app are sold anywhere else. Its network declaration is complete. It lists every server the app contacts on its own, and every transfer of personal data to these servers is described in my privacy policy. It is not export-controlled. It does not break or weaken encryption, it is not made to monitor, intercept or secretly access the communications or devices of others, and users cannot add their own encryption or change how it works beyond the settings it offers. Standard encryption, for example HTTPS, encrypted files or a password manager, is fine. If one of these points does not hold for your app, write to contact@crela.io before you submit it.

tools.name: check_review_status
tools.description: Poll the lightweight review status of a submitted software (progress, sub-step, rate-limit budget). Returns { tool_id, tool_status, awaiting_media, missing_media, presentation, next_step, version, review_job_status, review_sub_step, review_passed, rejection_reason, review_started_at, review_completed_at, rate_limit }. awaiting_media true means the tool is approved but not listed yet because screenshots are missing (missing_media); upload them and it is listed on its own. presentation attests the listing: level "incomplete" (below the minimum of 2 screenshots), "minimum" (listed) or "ideal", with toward_ideal listing the concrete steps left (logo, 4 screenshots of at least 1280 px width, video). Aim for "ideal" before you stop. Polling: poll every 30 s until review_job_status is neither "queued" nor "running"; a full review takes 5-15 minutes. If review_passed is true: the tool is approved; it is listed as soon as awaiting_media is false. If review_passed is false after completion: call get_review_report for structured findings, fix the reported issues, then call update_software with the fixed build and poll again. Use get_review_report only after polling is done, not for live progress. Also shows rate_limit.updates_remaining_today so you know your budget before calling update_software, and rate_limit.window_resets_at shows when the update budget resets. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: get_review_report
tools.description: Fetch the full review report of a submitted software: pass/fail, rejection reasons and structured findings to fix. Heavier than check_review_status — call this only after the review pipeline has completed, not for live progress polling. Findings are capped at 10 locations each (a CVE finding can carry hundreds of near-identical ones); the response then sets truncated:true and locations_omitted per finding. Raise max_locations_per_finding when you actually need the long tail. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

max_locations_per_finding.description: How many locations to keep per finding, default 10

tools.name: set_metadata
tools.description: Change metadata (title, description, price, categories, tags, etc.) of an existing software — no binary upload, no ZIP. DO NOT use this to upload a new build — use update_software for that. On an approved tool, a new title, description or long_description gets a quick automatic text check: it goes live at once, or the response has text_check with outcome "rejected" and a reason, and the current text stays. Changing categories or age_rating, or upgrading price_eur from 0 to a paid value, triggers a re-review; text changed in the same update waits for it. All other fields (tags, price reductions, tool_languages, unlisted) do NOT trigger re-review. Set unlisted:true to take an approved tool off the market (reversible with unlisted:false) — existing buyers keep access, it just cannot be newly purchased. Rate limit: 5 updates per tool per 24 h (shared with update_software). check_review_status shows your remaining budget. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

price_eur.description: 0 for free, or at least 0.50 (the smallest amount our payment provider can charge)

sale_price_eur.description: Discounted price (at least 0.50 and below price_eur); null ends the sale. Buyers see the lowest price of the 30 days before the sale crossed out

sale_ends_at.description: ISO timestamp when the sale ends; null = open-ended

trial_enabled.description: Enable a time-limited trial for a paid tool

license.description: Leave it unset in almost all cases. An open source license (SPDX identifier) can only be set with the first submission; here only the unchanged value or an empty string (back to the Crela Standard EULA) is accepted.

drm_mode.description: Paid tools are forced to sdk_required server-side regardless of this

framework.description: Usually auto-detected from the build; override only if wrong

tool_languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of every language the software user interface is available in, e.g. ["en","de"]; replaces the whole list. NOT the programming language - this drives the lang filter in search_software and the language chips on the listing page.

platforms.description: Correct the platforms when the ZIP auto-detection got them wrong

privacy_policy.description: Privacy policy text; null clears it. KO_09 rejects a build whose code contacts an analytics or telemetry service that this text does not name - this is the only way to satisfy that rule.

support_contact.description: Support contact shown to buyers, e.g. an email address; null clears it

security_updates_until.description: Date until which you provide security updates (YYYY-MM-DD), at least two years from today; five years recommended. Shown to buyers before they buy. Required for paid tools, optional for free tools. Can be changed but not removed; a paid listing without it must set it before its next version, and a free tool needs it before it becomes paid

safety_notes.description: Warnings and safety information buyers need, e.g. flashing lights or changes to system settings (plain text, max 2000 characters). Shown on the product page; null clears it

network_mode.description: Network allowlist mode: "none" = the app needs no network, "declared" = it only talks to the hosts in network_hosts, "user_chosen" = the user picks the servers (SSH, database, RSS or download clients). The Crela launcher starts the app behind a local proxy that logs every connection and blocks hosts outside the list; with "user_chosen" nothing is blocked. null clears it. Applies from the next build.

network_hosts.description: Hosts your app connects to, e.g. ["api.example.com", "*.cdn.example.com"]. A wildcard covers subdomains of your own domain only. Every host that receives user or device data must also be named in privacy_policy (KO_09). Applies from the next build.

video_url.description: https YouTube/Vimeo link; null removes the video entry

unlisted.description: true = take off market (hidden, not purchasable); false = re-list

age_rating.description: Games only, required before a game is listed (German JMStV). Send together with age_rating_source, age_rating_reasons and age_rating_questionnaire. For now Crela only offers games rated 0 (without an age restriction); 6 or higher is refused until Crela has a youth protection officer, 18 needs an age check. A person at Crela checks every game before it is listed.

age_rating_source.description: Where the age rating comes from: self (your own assessment), usk, pegi or iarc

age_rating_reasons.description: Reasons for the age rating, e.g. "fantasy violence without blood"; required from 6

violence.description: Fighting or violence, including cartoon or fantasy violence

fear.description: Scary or threatening scenes, horror or a frightening atmosphere

language.description: Crude language, insults or discriminating content

drugs.description: Alcohol, tobacco or drugs shown or mentioned

gambling.description: Gambling, simulated gambling or loot boxes

contact.description: Players can chat with or contact other players

age_rating_questionnaire.description: Games only: answer every content question truthfully (true = the game contains it). Any true answer rules out age rating 0.

tools.name: delete_software
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly delete one of your software items. Only works if it has never been sold — sold tools cannot be deleted (buyers keep their claim); take those off the market with set_metadata { unlisted: true } instead. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: get_my_software_details
tools.description: Read the full metadata and media list of one of your own software items by software_id. Works for all statuses (pending, approved, rejected). Returns { tool, media, missing_media, presentation } where media lists all uploaded screenshots/images with their ids and sizes, and presentation attests the listing level (incomplete, minimum, ideal) with toward_ideal, the steps left to the ideal presentation. Use this to verify current state after set_metadata, to get media ids before calling delete_media, or to read current metadata before an update. Unlike get_software, this works with the internal software_id (not a public slug) and does not require the tool to be approved. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: delete_media
tools.description: Permanently delete a screenshot, logo or other media item from a software listing. Use get_my_software_details to get the media ids of uploaded files. Uploaded files (screenshots and logos) are also deleted from storage; video URL entries are only removed from the listing. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

media_id.description: The id of the media item (from get_my_software_details response)

tools.name: update_media
tools.description: Update a media item: the sort order of any item (lower sort_order appears first), or the URL of a video entry (https YouTube/Vimeo link only). url can only be changed for video entries; for screenshots delete and re-upload. This tool does not create entries: a video is added with set_metadata { video_url }, an image with upload_screenshot. Use get_my_software_details to get media ids. Provide at least one of sort_order/url. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

media_id.description: The id of the media item (from get_my_software_details response)

sort_order.description: Display position; lower values appear first

url.description: New video URL (video entries only; https YouTube/Vimeo)

tools.name: upload_screenshot
tools.description: Upload a screenshot or the logo for a software from a local file path. Valid types: "screenshot" (default) or "logo". Accepted formats: JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF, max 5 MB per image. Before a listing goes live it needs at least 2 screenshots of the real app (at least 640 x 360 px); the server rejects smaller images. The first screenshot doubles as the cover. A logo is recommended, not required: square, at least 256 x 256 px; without one the launcher shows the first letter of the title. The review approves the software on its own; an approved tool without the screenshots stays unlisted and is listed on its own after the upload. The response says what is still missing (missing) and whether the listing just went on the market (went_live). For the ideal presentation (logo, 4 or more screenshots of at least 1280 px width, a video) read presentation.toward_ideal from check_review_status. The response also says where the image appears (placement, where): always in the media stage at the top of the product page, and also in a block once set_product_page places it there. Use delete_media to remove an uploaded image, update_media to reorder. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the image on disk

tools.name: upload_clip
tools.description: Upload a short preview clip for a software from a local MP4 file. It plays muted when someone points at the card on crela.io, so show the app in use from the first second. MP4 with H.264 video, landscape 16:9 (at least 1280 x 720 px), 3 to 60 seconds, max 80 MB; 15 to 30 seconds work best. Crela hosts the clip itself and does not convert it: export it as H.264 MP4. The file is checked on your disk first (codec, length, size), so a clip Crela would refuse is not uploaded. A new clip replaces the old one and keeps its place on the product page. Use delete_media to remove it. The response says where the clip appears (placement, where): at the top of the product page, or in a clip block if set_product_page placed one. A clip counts toward the ideal presentation (presentation.toward_ideal in check_review_status). Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the MP4 file on disk

tools.name: get_product_page
tools.description: Read the product page of one of your software items as set_product_page writes it: blocks (what visitors see), pending_blocks (your text changes waiting for review), media (every upload with id, type, size and where it appears), unplaced (screenshots in no block; they still show in the media stage at the top), hero (the clip at the top of the page), cover (the image on cards and launcher tiles), presentation (listing level with toward_ideal) and warnings (dead media ids, missing description block, no clip). Read it before set_product_page to get the media ids, and again afterwards to check that warnings is empty. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

tools.name: set_cover
tools.description: Choose one of your uploaded screenshots as the cover: the 16:9 image on website cards and launcher tiles. Without a chosen cover the first screenshot is used. Landscape, at least 1280 x 720 px. zoom (1 to 3) and focal_x/focal_y (0 to 1, the point that stays in view) set the crop; media_id null resets to the first screenshot. Get media ids from get_product_page. Requires CRELA_API_KEY.

media_id.description: Id of an uploaded screenshot, or null to reset

focal_x.description: Horizontal point that stays in view, 0 (left) to 1 (right), default 0.5

focal_y.description: Vertical point that stays in view, 0 (top) to 1 (bottom), default 0.5

stderr: [crela-mcp] ready on stdio - https://crela.io, no CRELA_API_KEY set: search tools work, every publish tool will fail with 401. Run npx -y @crela/mcp setup to connect your Crela account
